A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same correlation-sampling and cascaded optical-flow research despite the title change. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, figures, and code listings support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original sampling-pattern measurements, runtime and memory benchmarks, component ablations, and optical-flow evaluations on Charge, Spring, Sintel, and KITTI.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments with the revised sampler, Charge and Kubric-8K evaluations, and additional inference-strategy analyses.

M1.justification: V2 Section 4.3 introduces a fused sampler using per-thread block lists, inter-thread minimum voting, and immediate computation and sampling of correlation tiles. This avoids the explicit mask, globally stored blocks, and cross-iteration cache used by v1's implementation. The mathematical sampling target and main cascaded SEA-RAFT procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluated Kubric-8K scenes with generated moving objects, including accuracy and resource measurements in Tables 6-7. V1's ultra-high-resolution evaluation used only Charge's movie scenes. This substantially broadens the central high-resolution evaluation to another scene distribution; Charge, Spring, Sintel, and KITTI remain represented.

E2.justification: The Charge comparisons add DPFlow, ReCoVEr-CX, and WAFT and remove CCMR+ (v1 Tables 2/7 versus v2 Tables 1/11). The Spring/Sintel/KITTI comparison set is narrowed to RAFT, MS-RAFT+, SEA-RAFT, and newly added DPFlow. V2 Table 9 also evaluates a mixed default/on-demand sampler against the proposed sampler.

E3.justification: The main Charge comparison selects each method's lowest-1px-error resolution instead of its highest feasible resolution. V2 also introduces alternative low/high-resolution iteration budgets and changes the iteration/channel sweeps from 256 x 112 to 512 x 224 feature maps. The latter is supported by Section 9.1 and Table 10, although Section 5.1 inconsistently retains the earlier default.

E4.justification: V2 Table 9 adds tests of whether reallocating iterations toward lower resolutions or mixing existing samplers can reproduce the proposed efficiency benefits. The original caching ablation is removed, and the component analysis is replaced by measurements of fused-kernel stages using early exits (Section 8.4, Table 4). Resolution, iteration, feature-dimension, and hardware sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify one run per image for isolated benchmarking and report means and standard deviations across image samples, including shaded standard deviations in plots. V2 adds no repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure; changed uncertainty values retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Sampler timings and memory measurements are extensively replaced: at corresponding GH200 8K-input/1024-feature width, reported values change from 1004 ms and 15384 MB to 347 ms and 2829 MB. Charge results also change, including full-resolution RAFT EPE from 45.56 to 59.94 pixels, while cascaded SEA-RAFT retains 13.3% 1px error and 2.70-pixel EPE. Kubric and inference-strategy results are added; auxiliary-dataset accuracy entries are removed. Main-table changes also reflect the revised resolution-selection rule.

T1.justification: V1 Section 8.3 derives O(P^1.5) memory with block size B=P^(1/8). V2 Section 8.5 replaces this with separate time and memory derivations that are linear in pixel count for fixed sampling parameters. It also revises the requested-block bound to account for the bilinear sampling footprint, obtaining at most nine blocks per pixel for r=4 and B=8.

C1.justification: The central efficiency claim changes from a subquadratic-space speed/memory trade-off to linear time and space with memory comparable to on-demand sampling. Abstract maxima change from 90%/95%/50% to 92%/99%/63% for sampling runtime, memory, and end-to-end savings. V2 drops the first reference-based ultra-high-resolution evaluation claim and emphasizes the accuracy/runtime Pareto frontier.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific qualifications: only the forward pass is optimized, and the default sampler can remain faster at some small sizes on particular GPUs. Section 9.4 attributes Kubric's preference for lower-resolution inference to less-detailed objects. V1's discussion of cache overhead and future kernel fusion is replaced by interpretation of the fused implementation.

D1.justification: V2 adds actual CuTe DSL implementation listings, including GEMM helpers, sampling functions, and the fused kernel. It documents Ampere targeting, bfloat16 inputs, float32 accumulation, MMA instruction sizes, and shared-memory/register handling beyond v1's pseudocode and implementation outline. The Blender setup script is retained, but the explicit Spring subvalidation-split disclosure disappears.

R1.justification: Related work receives a targeted update with DPFlow, ReCoVEr, and WAFT. V2 acknowledges DPFlow's concurrent synthetic 8K evaluation and discusses cost-volume-free approaches, qualifying the earlier evaluation-novelty positioning. The broader positioning as an exact, RAFT-compatible correlation operator remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten around operator efficiency, and Section 4 is reorganized from separate mask/computation/sampling/cache subsections into high-level and fused implementations. Component analysis moves from the main evaluation to the method supplement, whose explanatory structure is expanded and reorganized. These changes exceed the title and terminology edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the qualitative teaser with an accuracy/runtime comparison, and Figure 4 gains a fused-execution diagram. V2 adds a block-mask illustration and resolution-dependent comparison plots, changes plot axes and scales, and restructures several tables. The same three appendix image examples are retained with revised comparator rows, rather than constituting new case studies.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's acknowledged mask/cache overhead bottleneck through a documented fused design and supporting measurements. A second 8K scene distribution, contemporary comparators, alternative-strategy controls, and best-resolution comparisons strengthen the empirical case, while kernel listings materially improve reproducibility. Conflicting default-size descriptions and omitted Spring split information reduce clarity, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in technical completeness and validation.
